messages.author: 8aa9b8cc06fdc99c
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] Compiling error (again...)
parts:
On 10/1/13 10:50 AM, Carlos wrote:
> GOOD NEWS! I installed it successfully and it compiles! Now I am dealing with providing initial values, because I guess
> that the model is a bit too complicated so STAN has some trouble finding initial values and a reasonable step size.

Do you have all the parameters constrained in their declaration
to match the support of their distributions in the model?

Some problems are too hard for random inits, at least the way
we're doing them now. We're about to get more serious about adaptation
and see if we can do better. One thing that's in 2.0 is allowing
a smaller interval around 0. Did you try init=0? Sometimes that'll
work even when initializing randomly around 0 won't (this is on
the unconstrained scale, so unconstrained vars get initialized to 0,
positive constrained to 1, interval constrained to middle of interval,
simplex to uniform, etc.)

> But
> that is something that I have to play with. Thanks a ton for all your help!
>
> You should send it to the list before spending a day on it!
> (Of course, sometimes you don't know it's going to take all
> day until it does.)
>
> As long as you have the model file and an indication of
> what the error is, we should be able to help pretty quickly.
>
>
> Well, I know that all of you are very busy, so I didn't want to disturb you so much, so I decided to spend time by
> myself trying to figure out if it was a problem with the code instead of a STAN bug. But thanks!

We try to prioritize helping users. As long as the problem's
easily reproducible, it doesn't take us much time. If it's not
an error we've seen before, then we really want to prioritize it,
because it may indicate an underlying bug somewhere.

- Bob
